name: Aam Digital
project_description: Aam Digital is used by social sector organizations that directly work with beneficiaries on the ground. As a customizable software platform, it is contributing to the work of organizations working towards a number of SDGs: Projects use Aam Digital to track & coordinate - living conditions and interventions to improve livelihoods (SDG 1); - beneficiaries' health status and health-related activities (SDG 3); - student support programs, learning progress, and attendance at educational activities (SDG 4); - work focused on gender equity and girls' rights (SDG 5); - activities of capacity building for SMEs and their outcomes (SDG 8); - work with marginalized communities (SDG 10) - activities to overcome conflict and stereotypes (SDG 16) - with its data management and reporting Aam Digital provides an easy way to evaluate and communicate work between partnerships across the globe with transparency and accountability (SDG 16)

name: Accessible Kazakhstan
project_description: The 'Accessible Kazakhstan' map reflects the needs of those who particularly seek accessible, safe and comfortable public space, including people with disabilities, parents with small children in prams, the elderly, pregnant women, temporarily injured people and children under seven years old. When monitoring a public facility, the owner of the facility is present, and the project team immediately notifies him or her of which elements of the facility do not meet the standards for accessibility of facilities open to the public. On the portal “Accessible Kazakhstan” one can find checklists with criteria for assessing accessibility of facilities, so that, if desired, the owners can read them and afterwards be involved in monitoring independently. Upon request, the project team develops recommendations, on the basis of which owners and government agencies start working on the adaptation of particular facilities for the aforementioned categories of citizens. Based on current data on accessibility of public facilities, comprehensive policies and plans for inclusion can be adopted and implemented. This, in turn, will reduce inequalities and accelerate achievement of other Sustainable Development Goals that affect development of an inclusive society. The world community needs qualified specialists who are able to form a barrier-free environment. It is for the purpose of training such specialists in 2019 within the framework of the “Accessible Kazakhstan” project that a unique online course “Ensuring accessibility of a public facility” was developed. The course: helps to get acquainted with legislation governing the provision of access to public facilities for people with disabilities and other population groups with limited mobility; can be used to find out what criteria accessibility of public facilities and open spaces is evaluated by; explains how to protect one’s right to a barrier-free environment; teaches how to monitor a public facility and develop recommendations for its adaptation to the needs of people with disabilities.

name: Accessible Medical Records via Integrated Technologies
project_description: AMRIT directly contributes to SDG 3 by enhancing access to quality primary healthcare through digital tools that empower frontline health workers. By enabling real-time access to Electronic Health Records (EHR), supporting noncommunicable disease management, maternal and child health services, and facilitating telemedicine, AMRIT addresses targets like reducing maternal mortality (3.1), combating communicable and noncommunicable diseases (3.3, 3.4), and achieving universal health coverage (3.8). AMRIT supports SDG 10 by bridging healthcare access gaps for rural and underserved populations. Through features like offline functionality, integration with Mobile Medical Units (MMUs), and multilingual support, AMRIT ensures equitable healthcare delivery, reducing disparities in health outcomes (10.2, 10.3).

name: AccessMod
project_description: AccessMod contributes to SDG target 3.8: achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC) by ensuring that all people have a physical access to the health services they need where they need them. It has been used in more than 40 low- and middle-income countries, and also in support of national health authorities and international health programs and organizations (WHO, UNFPA, UNICEF, The Global Fund, The World Bank, IDB, FIND).

name: Advocacy Training for Community Health Workers
project_description: SDG3: Good Health and Well-Being: CHWs are some of the most accessible and trusted frontline care providers in the world, especially in traditionally medically-underserved communities. By supporting these impactful workers, we support progress toward the Good Health and Well-Being targets by extending access to basic public health and primary care in vulnerable communities. SDG8: Decent Work and Economic Growth: Many CHWs are unpaid and do not receive adequate support and training. Our advocacy training equips CHWs with the skills to push for inclusion in decision-making conversations to advocate for their rights.

name: African Storybook
project_description: The African Storybook is composed of 4269 storybooks and 8098 translations available in 242 languages which provides open access to picture storybooks in the languages of Africa and many others for children’s literacy, enjoyment, and imagination. This is in line with SDG4: Quality Education and its target 4.1 Free primary and secondary education and 4.2 Equal access to quality pre-primary education. There are also reviews and descriptions of African Storybook at: - This review stresses the importance of quality storybooks in indigenous languages which is one of the features of ASb A published research article on ASb can be found here

name: AGRIS Open Data Set
project_description: The AGRIS Open Data Set includes a significant subset (around 50% as of July 2024) of the bibliographic records contributed by the AGRIS network of data providers to the AGRIS database, across all topics in the areas covered by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). Sharing publications’ metadata (and in many cases the link to the full text) enhances the reuse of research outputs and knowledge sharing across repositories and institutions, which is essential to make and monitor progress towards the SDGs: in the case of AGRIS, particularly the SDGs that have indicators for which FAO is the custodian UN agency. FAO is the custodian UN agency for 21 indicators and is a contributing agency to 5 more, spanning SDGs 1, 2, 5, 6, 12, 14 and 15.

name: AgriTech Observatory
project_description: SDG2- AgriTech Observatory serves as a knowledge hub for promoting digital agriculture innovations and policy development, thus enabling practical implementation of these technologies to increase agricultural efficiency and sustainability. SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure – The platform encourages the adoption of digital technologies, helping to modernize agricultural practices, support innovation, and strengthen infrastructure for sustainable agriculture. SDG 12: Responsible Consumption and Production – Digital tools, among those highlighted in the platform, can optimize resource use, minimize waste, and promote sustainable practices. SDG 13: Climate Action – By tracking and promoting climate-smart agricultural practices, the Observatory contributes to adaptation and mitigation strategies, helping farmers address climate change impacts. SDG 15: Life on Land – Sustainable digital agriculture practices can improve soil health, biodiversity, and ecosystem conservation, supporting the protection and restoration of terrestrial ecosystems. SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals – The Observatory is built upon collaboration with several institutions, including JengaLab, the Central European University, the American University of Central Asia, the Georgian Farmers Association, and the Digital AgriHub.

name: Agrontology
project_description: The Agrontology adds a semantic layer to any agri-food vocabulary (or dataset), providing domain-specific properties for concepts in the areas covered by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). Domain-specific semantic relations improve data and information exchange across repositories and institutions, which is essential to make and monitor progress towards the SDGs: in the case of the Agrontology, particularly the SDGs that have indicators for which FAO is the custodian UN agency. FAO is the custodian UN agency for 21 indicators and is a contributing agency to 5 more, spanning SDGs 1, 2, 5, 6, 12, 14 and 15.

name: AGROVOC Multilingual Thesaurus
project_description: AGROVOC facilitates the exchange and consolidation of knowledge, information, and data in the domains covered by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO). Consistent use of relevant concepts to index data and resources across repositories and institutions is essential to monitor progress on the SDGs: in the case of AGROVOC, particularly the SDGs that have indicators for which FAO is the custodian UN agency. FAO is the custodian UN agency for 21 indicators and is a contributing agency to 5 more, spanning SDGs 1, 2, 5, 6, 12, 14, and 15. Not only does AGROVOC cover all domains related to the SDGs for whose indicators FAO is custodian, but it also includes a dedicated concept for the SDGs and individual sub-concepts for each SDG, with official definitions ( This helps information and data managers correctly classify resources against the SDGs, and researchers and the general public easily find and browse SDG-related resources and data. AGROVOC is used to index content and data in many information systems relevant to SDGs 1, 2, 5, 6, 12, 14, and 15: library catalogs of agriculture/fisheries/nutrition/land research institutions and Ministries, repositories of the CGIAR centers, the FAO AGRIS database and various other FAO resources. Being a resource managed in partnership with several institutions all over the world, and being coordinated by FAO under the Partnerships and UN Collaboration Division, AGROVOC is particularly relevant to SDG 17.

name: Aid Management Platform
project_description: The Aid Management Platform (AMP) aligns with SDG 16's specific target 16.6 of "develop[ing] effective, accountable and transparent institutions at all levels" by providing governments and development partners with a tool that allows for both parties to conduct better resource planning, identify gaps and duplications in foreign assistance, better align foreign assistance to national priorities, and to make information about aid flows more transparent to civil society, citizens, journalists, researchers, and other stakeholders.

name: Altinn
project_description: It’s essential for governments and institutions to be able to have effective dialogue with its population an businesses using a trusted platform. Altinn is such a platform, used by every organisation and the whole population in Norway, since 2003.

name: Android FHIR SDK
project_description: Through this toolkit, we make it easier for developers to build mobile health applications specifically designed to meet the needs of low-resource settings, in particular in LMICs. Through our collaboration with the World Health Organization (WHO), we also enable the deployment of digitized clinical guidelines (SMART Guidelines) for improving the quality of care. In line with target 3.8 Achieve universal health coverage and 3.C Increase health financing and support health workforce in developing countries.

name: Apache Fineract
project_description: Apache Fineract is relevant to SDG 1 - End Poverty in All Forms because it makes available low-cost yet modern core banking infrastructure for managing wallets, savings/transactional accounts, share/equity accounts, loan/credit accounts, and more. It provides the critical infrastructure for delivering financial inclusion enabling financial service providers to focus on customer-facing innovation and advancing the financial health of their customers. Fineract advances SDG 16 by enabling financial institutions at the public and private sector levels to operate more efficiently and effectively but also be fully transparent in their operations disclosing the full cost of financial services, protecting data responsibly, and advancing financial literacy. Fineract advances SDG 17 - Partnership for these goals - because by providing open source core banking infrastructure it enables the creation of a commercial ecosystem of solution and support providers building innovations powered by the DPG serving local market need while contributing back upstream to create a virtuous cycle

name: Avni
project_description: SDG3 - Avni has been used across several organizations to provide primary healthcare, which includes family planning, mother-and-child care, adolescent health, NCDs, and in preventing alcoholism in rural and tribal settings within India. SDG4 - Avni has been used to digitise the WHO Teach tool that is being used by some state governments in India ( It is also used in rural settings (in Assam and Gujarat) to run programs that detect and stop child labor and promote school attendance. SDG6 - Avni is used in monitoring the construction of toilets in the urban slums of Maharashtra. It is used across multiple states of India to monitor annual waterbody desilting activities. It is also used in Bihar to monitor activities related to piped water supply.

name: Bahmni
project_description: Over 500 implementations across 50 countries - predominantly in Africa and Asia. Millions of patients across the world have benefited from Bahmni as their stretched doctors and caregivers have used the system to track and monitor patient health and records. The end TB project that tested the latest antibiotics (Bedqualine and Delamanid) was run on Bahmni. We have also collected a few case studies of impact by Bahmni adopters here: and here

name: Bebbo Parenting App
project_description: Bebbo promotes SDG 2, 3, 4 and 5. In particular, SDG indicator 2.2.1 (prevalence of childhood stunting), SDG indicator 2.2.2 (prevalence of childhood malnutrition (wasting or overweight)), SDG indicator 3.b.1 (proportion of the target population covered by all vaccines included in their national programme) and SDG indicator 4.2.1 (proportion of children aged 24–59 months (2-5 years) who are developmentally on track in health, learning and psychosocial well-being, by sex). These indicators are supported by providing parents with a rich library of well-researched articles and videos covering various domains of child health. The content is tailored and filtered based on the child's profile, offering personalized recommendations. It covers health and vaccination, early learning protection and safety, nutrition and breastfeeding, and mental health and well-being of parents. The app also includes interactive tools to monitor and support the child's development, optimal growth, and health visits and immunization schedules. By providing accessible information and tools, Bebbo promotes the goal of ensuring a healthy child. In addition, Bebbo has been recognized as a gender transformative initiative by UNICEF. It provides content for fathers and encourages their active involvement in the upbringing of the child. The app promotes increased engagement of both parents in a gender transformative way, supporting the goal of achieving gender equality and empowering all women and girls and hence supports SDG Indicator 5.4.1 (proportion of time spent on unpaid domestic and care work, by sex, age and location).

name: Bisa Health
project_description: Bisa health platform allows the public access to doctors and receive healthcare information through their mobile devices (both smart and non-smart phones). This is an advantage to people who need medical care and advice but are not able to visit the hospital for various reasons such as poverty, delays because of long queues at the hospital and the fear of stigmatization, especially for people who have symptoms of Sexually Transmitted Diseases (STDs), which makes them embarrassed to seek the needed treatment., Bisa has partnered with GIZ ( The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit GmbH ) and the Ghana Health Services to enhance Ghana’s public health service education of COVID-19 and manage affected cases who are self-isolating. The Bisa App provides patients direct access to doctors and health practitioners with a click of the App, doctors are readily available to respond to all questions within minutes with absolutely no cost involved. The Bisa App is instrumental in these times because it will reduce face-to-face doctor consultations and help with reducing congestion in hospitals.

name: Boxtribute
project_description: Our platform's most classic use targets SDG indicators 1.3-1.5, which includes providing basic services to people in poverty and other vulnerable situations, as well as improving the resilience of communities to disasters and other shocks, Much of our work has to do with the distribution of non-food items (NFI), in particular clothing and shelter items, which are often donated by the public when they no longer suit the needs of the individual. Through our work, we allow many household items that are otherwise in good condition to be redirected away from landfill and waste, towards providing for the core needs of vulnerable people. Without our platform, many community groups would have no way of organizing the donated goods and matching that to the needs of the population. One of the key aspects of our work and in our platform is around encouraging collaboration and interdependence between public interest actors, particularly humanitarian aid actors. We are rolling out in our design the ability for organizations not only to store and distribute aid, but also transfer that aid between each other in a collaborative and cooperative way.

name: caMicroscope
project_description: The primary use case of caMicroscope is related to SDG Indicator 3.b.2 (Development assistance to medical research & basic healthcare). The caMicroscope platform is designed specifically to enable customizable medical studies for biomedical imaging. This typically takes the form of patholgist studies; for example see The research itself generally aims to help with SDG Indicator 3.4.1 (Reduce Mortality rate from non-communicable diseases) by focusing on cancer early detection studies.

name: Care | Open Healthcare Network
project_description: Care is an integrated tele-triage+bed allocation+patient shifting+teleICU tool for implementing a decentralised healthcare management strategy. Our goal is to continuously improve the quality and accessibility of healthcare services using digital tools. The tool help states achieve Universal Health Coverage by making healthcare accessible to population closer to home, thereby reducing cost of healthcare and the out-of-pocket expenses borne by the patients. The tool also enables collaborative care delivery between the tertiary and secondary tier through TeleICU solution, improving the overall health outcomes in the peripheries including improving the health outcomes of mother and child, management of communicable and non communicable diseases, allows smaller hospitals to respond better to trauma cases etc. Its pandemic management module also allows early detection of disease outbreaks and aids in better management of capacity and healthcare resources in such regions. CARE exemplifies "SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals" through Target 17.7 and 17.17. CARE is a great example of a sustainable technology available for adoption in developing counties. Moreover through its collaborative model of software development and implementation, the project units developers, students, healthcare professionals, and government bodies. This partnership approach amplifies the impact of healthcare innovations and supports the achievement of targets across multiple SDGs by leveraging collective expertise and resources.

name: Cboard
project_description: Cboard is relevant to SDG 3 by acting as a therapeutic and health-assistive tool that directly impacts the quality of life and mental health of people with disabilities. Target 3.4 (Mental Health & Well-being): Inability to communicate often leads to extreme frustration, depression, and social isolation. Cboard provides a "voice," reducing the psychological burden of speech impairments and fostering a sense of agency and emotional well-being. Cboard is a critical tool for "Inclusive Education," ensuring that children with disabilities are not left behind in the classroom. Target 4.5 (Equal Access for the Vulnerable): This target aims to ensure equal access to all levels of education for persons with disabilities. Cboard allows children who cannot speak to participate in lessons, answer questions, and interact with peers, which is essential for their integration into mainstream schools. Target 4.a (Disability-Sensitive Learning Environments): Cboard transforms standard digital devices (tablets, laptops) into inclusive learning tools. It is used in pilot programs (notably in Croatia, Montenegro, and Serbia) to train teachers and special educators on how to support students with complex communication needs. Cboard addresses the "digital divide" and the high cost of assistive technology. Target 10.2 (Social and Economic Inclusion): By empowering individuals to express their needs and opinions, Cboard facilitates their participation in the social, political, and eventually economic life of their communities. Target 10.3 (Ensuring Equal Opportunity): Traditional AAC devices can cost thousands of dollars, creating a massive inequality gap where only wealthy families or those in developed nations can afford them. As a free web app, Cboard levels the playing field for users in low-resource settings. Impact in Serbia, Croatia, and Montenegro

name: cfr
project_description: crf contributes to timely and accurate epidemiological insights, allowing decision-makers to respond to health crises more quickly and effectively, thus supporting the goal of achieving better health outcomes. As part of the Epiverse initiative, cfr underscores the importance of Partnerships for the Goals by relying on open-source collaborations and international partnerships to develop and maintain tools like crf. This collaborative approach enhances the accessibility and effectiveness of public health interventions, aligning with the SDGs' broader objective of fostering global cooperation for sustainable development.

name: Chamilo
project_description: By empowering potential teachers with an easy to use digital tool to provide ubiquitous access to their teaching material to anyone, we allow anyone to share material that will allow other people to learn, self-evaluate and become active contributors of a better world. We also empower the potential teachers to improve their material over time by collecting feedback and editing their content accordingly, which helps provide better quality education. Quality education usually leads (indirectly or directly) to better income, which reduces poverty, improves economic growth, reduces inequalities and allow for better implementation of justice and peace.

name: Cider
project_description: Cider's purpose is to improve the targeting of humanitarian aid and thereby help alleviate poverty, especially the most extreme poverty. Well-targeted aid is an important tool for poverty reduction in pursuit of SDG 1. As an example, Cider informed the Novissi aid program in Togo, which was carried out jointly by the non-profit GiveDirectly, the Togolese government, and the Global Policy Lab at UC Berkeley. Researchers involved found that Cider's poverty predictions were more accurate than predictions we could have obtained using any viable alternative considered, given the time and resource constraints of the program. This increased accuracy enabled funds to be directed to poorer individuals and households. Details of the program, Cider's role in it, and evaluations of effectiveness can be found in Aiken et al (2022)

name: CIEL terminology
project_description: CIEL is primarily designed to help with the assessment of health problems, the implementation of health interventions and evaluation of health indicators (therefore most closely associated with SDG3). CIEL is also designed to empower communities and underserved areas by ensuring that the information systems are sensitive to their needs. Its multi-lingual, multi-national data dictionary allows for sharing of best practices and data to improve representation of LMICs and underrepresented populations in national reporting, research and care delivery.

name: CityLearn
project_description: CityLearn allows to work out how end-use energy demand can be shifted throughout the day. This helps aligning demand with availability of renewable energy resources (solar, wind), which reduces the reliance on fossil fuel powered thermal power generators. A specific problem of reducing cost, emissions and providing grid services has been used in the 2022 CityLearn Challenge here CityLearn can be generalized to a variety of use cases though. It is the only tool that allows to work out demand-side energy shifting at scale.

name: CKAN
project_description: While CKAN is used by many different organizations tackling many different challenges related to the SDGs, it is specially used to help attain SDG 16 (Promote just, peaceful, and inclusive societies). Perhaps the target most contributes to is 16.10 (Ensure public access to information and protect fundamental freedoms) by providing a free, community-led tool for official institutions to publish their data, which is easy to use for users and provides capabilities for advanced users to monitor and explore the datasets. Being widely used by government and civil society institutions to publish open data, it also helps attain among others target 16.6 (Develop effective, accountable, and transparent institutions) by helping publish data about official budgets, expenditures, declared interests etc, allowing citizens to hold institutions accountable. Other examples where CKAN helps meet the targets of the SDGs include CKAN being used by UNHCR to centralize and standardize refugee-related data, helping with target 10.7 (Facilitating orderly, safe, regular, and responsible migration and mobility of people), and by UNOCHA to host humanitarian data, as well as by several other non-profit organizations working on tackling inequalities around the world (SDG1, SDG10). It is also trusted by many government institutions to publish data that is critical for transparency, accountability and that promotes economic growth (SDG11, SDG8, SDG16). Other organizations like Energinet in Denmark use CKAN to publish energy-related data (SDG7).

name: ClimWeb
project_description: SDG: SDG 13: Climate Action - This is the most directly relevant SDG. ClimWeb directly supports climate action by: Enabling early warning systems for climate-related disasters, facilitating climate data sharing and evidence-based decision-making, supporting climate adaptation and mitigation strategies Improving climate resilience through better information delivery.

name: Code Your Future
project_description: Code Your Future is a free training programme for refugees and other people excluded from education and training. Our classes are free, and our teachers are volunteers. Our free and open-source syllabus is developed and published directly on GitHub. We collaborate with other free code programmes within the MigraCode network ( and ad-hoc in the UK, South Africa, Roma, Medellin, etc. We do our work in public. We are committed to free, open-source education and curriculum development, and all our materials are published and shared freely. People use our syllabus alone, in a code group, within another coding programme, and within our in-person classes. Code Your Future is a learning community where total life transformation happens. We understand that transformational change must be challenging but should not be harmful. Our course recognises that change can be difficult. We create spaces of psychological safety, including online spaces, where people can feel supported during a challenging learning journey to starting careers in tech. Our work largely falls on these targets in SDG 4: - Target 4.3: Equal access to affordable technical, vocational and higher education - Target 4.4: Increase the number of people with relevant skills for financial success - Target 4.5: Eliminate all discrimination in education. Our work also supports these targets: 5.5 Effective participation and access to the ICT industry and cutting-edge technology. 40% of our trainees are women, while only 12.5% of software engineers in the UK are women. 8.5.1 Hourly earnings & 10.2.1 People living below 50 per cent of median income. 99% of our trainees are on a low income and 83% live in poverty. Graduates from CYF typically move from 1st or 2nd decile income group to the 8th or 9th within six months of graduation.

name: CodeCarbon
project_description: CodeCarbon allow users to understand how much energy and CO2 emissions are associated with a computer process. Knowing that the user could relocate the process to a region with less carbon-intensive electricity or reduce the electricity consumption with optimisation (Target 12.2, 12.6).

name: CodiTeach
project_description: The CodiTeach platform contributes to Sustainable Development Goals 4 and 17. In particular, it relates to point 4.A - "enhancing the qualifications of teachers in developing countries". The platform offers a multifaceted management system that not only augments managerial competencies but also facilitates timely monitoring of student progress, thereby elevating the technological literacy of educators. Additionally, CodiTeach offers the capability for users to automatically integrate a wide array of curricula and materials, which are readily accessible for review and utilization in the educational process, significantly simplifying the preparation and execution of lessons. We believe that our platform significantly contributes to Goal 17.8 by facilitating the establishment of an innovation capacity-building mechanism tailored for the least developed nations, and by amplifying the deployment of enabling technologies. Our platform stands as an accessible and easy-to-use innovation, specifically designed for the least developed countries, effectively bridging the technological divide between advanced and emerging economies.

name: CommCare
project_description: This is the primary area of impact for CommCare. The platform is designed to empower frontline health workers (FHWs) to deliver more effective care in low-resource settings. Target 3.1 & 3.2 (Maternal and Child Mortality): CommCare is widely used for prenatal and postnatal tracking. Studies in countries like Guatemala and Tanzania have shown that their decision-support tools help frontline workers increase the rate of in-facility births and reduce maternal and infant mortality. Target 3.3 (Communicable Diseases): The platform is a "Global Good" for managing infectious diseases. It has been used for the Ebola and COVID-19 response, as well as for tracking HIV treatment and malaria prevention. Target 3.8 (Universal Health Coverage): By providing a "Precision Tasking Framework," CommCare helps community health workers reach underserved populations, ensuring that even remote communities gain access to essential health services. Target 2.2 (End all forms of malnutrition): CommCare is the most commonly used mobile platform for nutrition-related interventions. In India, it has been deployed at a massive scale (reaching over 500,000 workers) to monitor child growth. The CommCare Evidence Base has more than 100, peer-reviewed studies that speak to third-party impact of CommCare across numerous SDGs

name: Community Health Toolkit
project_description: Medic’s work aligns with SDGs 3, 5, and 17. SDG 3: Our mission is rooted in achieving good health and well-being for all. We strive to advance universal health coverage through our digital solutions and our work actively supports the professionalization of CHWs to deliver these critical services. The CHT goes beyond simple communication; it allows CHWs to track patients and health data, ensuring proper care coordination and follow-up, for example, guiding CHWs to high-risk pregnancies or missed vaccinations. Disease surveillance functions allow CHWs to serve as an early warning system for epidemics. Evidence on the impact of CHT interventions is available here: and via our research archive: SDG 5: Medic and the CHT community’s advocacy for gender equality is most apparent in our advocacy for better compensation, protective equipment, and support for the mostly female CHWs who are the main users of CHT apps. Examples include a journal article in the BMJ calling for greater involvement of and protection of CHWs in COVID-19 response ( and participation in a report (lead author: Resolve to Save Lives) focused on protecting health workers ( SDG 17: The CHT is recognized as a digital public good, and the public goods approach is all about partnering to achieve the SDGs rather than going alone with a private/proprietary solution. The CHT is included as a digital public good in Digital Square’s Global Goods Guidebook ( and is featured as a global good in a USAID, WHO, and ITU supported course in Digital Health: Planning National Systems (

name: Compar:IA
project_description: In line with SDG 4 (Quality Education), compar:IA is widely used in educational contexts to teach students and practitioners about AI plurality, bias, and environmental impact, helping foster digital literacy. With respect to SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), Compar:IA plays a key role in supporting innovation by providing open datasets that act as foundational infrastructure for building more robust AI models in under-represented languages. Finally, in connection with SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), the platform raises awareness of the environmental costs of AI usage, encouraging more sustainable and responsible practices across the AI ecosystem.

name: Compar:IA Datatsets
project_description: SDG4: Quality Education Compar:IA datasets support education and capacity building in AI by providing open, real-world conversational data and human preference annotations in French. They are used for teaching, research, and public AI literacy, especially for audiences outside English-dominated resources. SDG9: Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure The datasets provide open digital infrastructure for AI research and development, enabling innovation in language technologies, benchmarking, and model evaluation. They lower barriers to entry for researchers, startups, and public institutions working on non-English AI systems. SDG10: Reduced Inequalities By producing large-scale French-language and non-English human preference data, compar:IA directly addresses linguistic and cultural inequalities in AI systems. The datasets help reduce the dominance of English-centric AI training data and improve model performance and alignment for under-resourced language communities. SDG16: Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions Compar:IA is developed within the public sector and publishes transparent, open datasets that support accountable and explainable AI. The datasets enable public oversight, independent evaluation of AI systems, and informed policy-making, strengthening trust in digital public institutions.

name: Connect For Life
project_description: Educational health content customized per disease can be shared through the Connect For Life platform with the targeted patient population and this can impact the following SDG targets: SDG 3.3.1: Using the communication from Connect For Life, patients can be stimulated to adhere to their HIV medication intakes and in so doing reduce their risk of transmission to other non-infected individuals. Educational content can also be shared in a discrete fashion to ensure that risks of transmission are known. This educational content can be important for many HIV patient groups such as adolescents, MSM, HIV-infected pregnant women to help prevent transmission to sexual contacts and or to unborn babies. SDG 3.3.2: For TB patients adherence to medication for longer treatment periods is critical to achieve cure. Messages from Connect For Life can take the form of engaging, actionable instructions to help motivate individuals to adhere to therapy and thereby help them to reach care and preventing further transmission.

name: Consul Democracy
project_description: Consul Democracy is used by governments globally on local, regional, and national levels to involve citizens in decision-making, helping to develop effective, accountable, and transparent institutions as well as ensuring responsive, inclusive, participatory, and representative decision-making at all levels. Transparency and accountability are further enhanced thanks to the open-source nature of Consul's development, which is community-based. More on the goals, the way we work and participating institutions can be read at: and Moreover, we support governments to work on all Sustainable Development Goals with their citizens. We have joined forces with The United Nations Development Programme and the cooperative Enreda to foster participation around the Agenda 2030 by incorporating a SDG module into the software so that entities around the world can use it in their Sustainable Development Goals localization processes.

name: Convexity Humanitarian Aid Transfer Solution (CHATS)
project_description: CHATS solution contributes to the advancement of the objectives of SDGs 2, 3, and 8 through its application in aid delivery and humanitarian assistance. For SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), CHATS facilitates the efficient distribution of food, cash, and life-saving materials to vulnerable populations, directly contributing to the reduction of undernourishment, reduction of food insecurity, and promoting knowledge and access to financial services. In the context of SDG 3 (Good Health and Well-being), CHATS improves the methodologies for the distribution of medication, promoting timely access to healthcare resources, and thereby addressing targets related to maternal and child health, disease prevention, and overall well-being. CHATS aligns with SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth) by streamlining aid distribution processes, improving livelihoods, and creating earning opportunities thereby fostering economic resilience within communities, further supporting targets associated with employment, economic growth, and the formalization of labor conditions.

name: cQube
project_description: Saral can be used across domains for applications that require quick and seamless phygitization of data - capture of physical data in a digital, structured format. This results in significant savings in terms of time and effort that would otherwise be required in order to capture the physical data in a digital format. Sunbird Saral has been successfully used by the state government of the largest state in India (Uttar Pradesh) to conduct state-wide assessments tests for about 17 million students from grade 1 to grade 8 - in order to garner a grassroots level understanding of the learning gaps, as well as the needs and challenges faced by the students. The state had a strong desire to gain a deeper understanding of student performance in order to effectively cater to various programs and student learning needs, which aim to achieve universal foundational literacy and numeracy in primary schools by 2025. However, traditional assessment methods bring forth several challenges - these methods were not at scale or student level, making it difficult to obtain reliable data for the state to make informed decisions. Additionally, the time it took for data to reach the central department from traditional assessment methods was too long, as the process involved physical question paper preparation, exam conduction, answer sheet evaluation, result generation and then manually digitizing results, leading to a delay of up to three to four months. The Saral solution replaces the old answer sheets with OMR-based answer sheets and allows teachers to scan the answer sheet through the Saral App. This process instantly digitizes data and allows the state to receive digitized data on the very same day of scanning. Quick and detailed information provided by Saral Assessments has empowered decision-makers to make data-driven choices and take prompt action to enhance educational outcomes in the state. The state is now also planning for a pilot program to explore the use of Saral for other teacher-led activities such as new student admissions to schools. The app can be used to quickly scan admission forms of students and transfer the data to the state backend systems, resulting in significant saving of time for the teachers.

name: Creative Commons Legal Tools
project_description: Creative Commons Legal Tools are related to several Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), primarily in the context of promoting access to knowledge, education, and innovation: SDG 4: Quality Education - Target 4.3: Creative Commons licenses promote open educational resources (OER), making quality education more accessible and affordable for all; Target 4.7: They support the dissemination of knowledge related to global citizenship, human rights, and sustainable development; SDG 9: Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure - Target 9.5: By enabling the open sharing of research and innovation, Creative Commons licenses support scientific research and technological innovation; Target 9.C: They also facilitate access to information and communications technology, contributing to universal and affordable access to the Internet; SDG 10: Reduced Inequalities - Target 10.2: Creative Commons licenses help reduce inequalities by ensuring that educational and cultural materials are accessible to all, regardless of economic status; SDG 16: Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions - Target 16.10: They promote access to information and protect fundamental freedoms by enabling the free flow of knowledge and cultural expression; SDG 17: Partnerships for the Goals - Target 17.6: Creative Commons licenses encourage global partnerships by facilitating the sharing of knowledge and innovation across borders; Target 17.8: They support the implementation of technology and innovation, particularly in developing countries, by making resources freely available; Creative Commons legal tools make it simple and free for the world's educators, scientists, researchers, journalists, artists, hardware and software designers, and others to build and share their digital solutions with the world as digital public goods.

name: CREDEBL
project_description: Governments are implementing decentralised digital identity to increase access to services for every beneficiary using the Web and mobile applications while emphasising on protecting the users' privacy. So that governments can pass the benefits (financial, education and health) directly to the beneficiaries. Both the public and private sector needs (decentralised) digital identity (AKA Self-Sovereign Identity) infrastructure to effectively organize, and in fact to build the digital societies of the future by being able to issue verifiable credentials and verify those.

name: Crosscut
project_description: Health program managers often miss coverage, equity, and cost goals because they cannot easily and affordably access quality information below the district level. Achieving these goals often involves costly, recurring technical assistance. The Crosscut app is a technology that helps to solve this problem by allowing non-technical health program staff to independently create catchment area maps, estimate target populations, analyze geographic accessibility, and make effective plans at the sub-district level. This “microplanning” helps to ensure settlements are not missed, services are provided equitably, and the right quantity of supplies is where they need to be. We aim to "de-expert" microplanning, and our vision is for any user to be able to quickly do geospatial microplanning without the need for outside experts.

name: Dalgo
project_description: Dalgo supports the social sector statistical capacity building in the nonprofits that use it. Our current nonprofit users work in the fields of water quality (SDG 6), early childhood education, K-12 education (SDG 4), vocational education, 21st-century skills (SDG 8), sanitation rights, and child and maternal health (SDG 3). By way of consolidation of intervention data collected from different sources, we enable nonprofits to generate holistic insights on their impact in these fields which inform their practice and communication of their impact. In line with SDG 9 target 9B - Support domestic technology development and industrial diversification: Dalgo also enables nonprofits to bring relevance to public data through the automated ingestion and processing of data from public data sources which is then made conveniently accessible to beneficiaries via on-ground or digital intervention (WhatsApp chatbots/webapps).

name: Data Norge
project_description: SDG9: Gathering and displaying data that may be shared can open up new possibilities for innovation and establishing new businesses by making it easier to find and reuse data that already exists. It is also possible for private sector to make a data catalog of their own to display the data they have that may be reused, and make it easier to collaborate between organizations in a county, and between countries. SDG16: By displaying public sector data, a portal/data catalog like this one can make it easier to reuse data between organizations in public sector, this sort of overview may also strengthen citizens' trust in the public sector.

name: Data Observation Toolkit
project_description: In 2019, the United Nations Statistical Commission stated: “Every misclassified or unrecorded death is a lost opportunity to ensure other mothers and babies do not die in the same way. When it comes to health, better data can be a matter of life and death.” DataKind developed the Data Observation Toolkit (DOT) in response to a gap in digital health solutions space to monitor health data generated by other digital tools for problems with data integrity, quality and other scenarios that might need attention. The toolkit aims to provide easier access to data monitoring without the need for deep technical skills.

name: Data to Policy Navigator
project_description: The most applicable are SDG 10 and SDG 17. In SDG 10, there is the relevance of policymakers taking action to create more equitable societies, as well as reducing the inequality of who can use and access data for policy. The Navigator is for all skill and technical levels and can help policymakers who have little expertise using data or a lot of expertise both achieve their goals of utilizing data for policy. SDG 17 is relevant through both creating partnerships with development organizations such as ourselves and policymakers, as well as contains a lot of information, particularly in the use case section, on how to form and build data partnerships for the SDGs.

name: Database of Greek and Latin Conjectural Emendations Attested in MSS
project_description: Classical studies is a discipline where data is usually scattered among expensive books and modern technology finds little use. By broadening access to an important set of research materials, this database increases the number of potential researchers per million inhabitants and brings web technology and CI/CD to bear on the field, thus contributing to the target of ‘Enhance research and upgrade industrial technologies’ (9.5). Being open-source, it also facilitates the target of ‘Equal access to affordable technical, vocational and higher education’ (4.3) by making the data available to people who may not have access to a university library.

name: Decidim
project_description: SDG10: Citizen participation mechanisms are traditionally held in person. Providing a digital channel for participation enables people who are home-bound, people who are busy at work when participatory events happen, or people who are otherwise unable to attend, to take part in participatory processes as well. SDG16: In order for participatory democracy processes to be legitimate, they need to be transparent and audited. Decidim provides transparency to each decision taken within a participatory process by making every vote, discussion, proposal and participation, open and published, so that a digital archive of the process remains for any needed audits. Decidim has also worked to implement traceability mechanisms against tampering which are reflected in Decidim's social contract

name: Deon
project_description: The checklist has explicit items to identify and mitigate biases (relevant to SDG 10). See here for particular items on identifying bias and reducing inequalities (SDG10)

name: Designsystemet
project_description: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions Target 16.6: Develop effective, accountable and transparent institutions at all levels Designsystemet enhances the efficiency and transparency of public digital services by offering reusable, accessible, and standardized components, patterns, and tools. It supports cross-agency collaboration and ensures consistent user experiences, helping institutions become more effective and accountable. Target 16.10: Ensure public access to information and protect fundamental freedoms By embedding universal design and accessibility into all components, Designsystemet ensures that everyone — including people with disabilities — has equitable access to public digital services and information, thereby supporting fundamental digital rights. SDG 17 – Partnerships for the Goals Target 17.6: Enhance regional and international cooperation on science, technology and innovation Designsystemet is published as open source under a permissive license, enabling reuse and adaptation beyond Norway. It encourages collaboration across public and private sectors and supports the global exchange of digital best practices. Target 17.18: Enhance capacity-building support to increase the availability of high-quality, timely and reliable data By providing clear design guidelines, accessibility support, and reusable digital infrastructure, Designsystemet improves the quality and consistency of public services. This contributes to more reliable and inclusive digital service delivery across sectors.

name: DEXA Protocol
project_description: The DEXA protocol facilitates sustainable personal exchange for organisations, ensuring that all data transactions are lawful, scalable and verifiable. An organisation can be a Data Source or a Data Using Service. The DEXA protocol brings in the requisite trust and governance to establish a ubiquitous data exchange marketplace while empowering individuals to control their data. All organisations need to ensure that they are on the right side of the law (e.g. the GDPR) when consuming personal data (risk management) and to establish the digital trust needed for individuals to say yes to sharing their data.

name: DHIS2
project_description: DHIS2 is the world's largest Health Management Information System platform, and is currently in use in more than 80 low- and middle-income countries, 74 are deployed at national scale. DHIS2 is also used by national health authorities and international health organizations (such as WHO, the CDC, PEPFAR, The Global Fund, Gavi) for management of specific health programs, such as HIV, TB, Malaria, immunization, and disease surveillance. The large-scale adoption of DHIS2 has enabled countries to leverage it to rapidly respond to emerging crises such as the Covid-19 pandemic. New DHIS2 tools for Climate & Health facilitate incorporation of climate, weather, and environmental data into DHIS2 to support analysis, modeling, and forecasting of climate-sensitive health risks and help improve the climate resilience of national health systems. DHIS2 has also developed a module for last-mile logistics intended for use at the health facility level and integrated with a central eLMIS or ERP. The features include report and transaction-based stock management, equipment management, and temperature monitoring. In addition to health, DHIS2 is also now being deployed as an Education Management Information System (EMIS) in several countries, which facilitates more effective triangulation of data between health and education programs (for example, vaccination campaigns targeting school-aged children), as well as supporting purely education-related goals.

name: DiCRA
project_description: The objective of the DiCRA platform is to provide free and open access to geospatial datasets through an open digital platform thereby enabling concrete evidence-driven policies and concerted action from all stakeholders involved in sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture. Through geospatial analysis and data-powered positive deviance approaches, the platform informs stakeholders on which farms are more resilient to extreme weather events. Indigenous knowledge is tapped through field validation and ethnography to suggest good practices on climate-resilient farming that are already working well through bottom-up approaches, to feed into large-scale agriculture programs and policies and optimize public investments in climate-resilient agriculture. DiCRA platform, therefore, contributes to SDG 2 to 'End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture'. Specifically, DiCRA contributes to SDG target 2.4 which states 'By 2030, ensure sustainable food production systems and implement resilient agricultural practices that increase productivity and production, that help maintain ecosystems, that strengthen capacity for adaptation to climate change, extreme weather, drought, flooding, and other disasters and that progressively improve land and soil quality. , DiCRA platform contributes to SDG 13 'Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts'. With its objective to enhance climate adaptation measures through data-driven approaches as well as the impact on policies for climate resilient agriculture, the DiCRA platform contributes directly to SDG target 13.1 'Strengthen resilience and adaptive capacity to climate-related hazards and natural disasters in all countries' and SDG target 13.2 to 'Integrate climate change measures into national policies, strategies and planning'.

name: DIGIT
project_description: SDG 9, our work is closely aligned with Target 9.1, "Develop quality, reliable, sustainable and resilient infrastructure, including regional and transborder infrastructure, to support economic development and human well-being, with a focus on affordable and equitable access for all". Effective local government, which is able to provide local infrastructure and services, is key to inclusive development at the last mile, and enabling local governments to collect resources and deliver services in an efficient & transparent manner enhances their capacity to deliver the conditions for well-being, sustainability, and innovation.    Our work also aligns with Target 9.c, leveraging local intermediaries to provide digitally-enabled access to services to populations that may otherwise have to rely on physical channels, or have difficulty accessing services at all., At eGov, we see our work as fitting with the themes of SDG 11 - Sustainable Cities and Communities - and SDG 17 - Partnerships for Development. SDG 11 - Some key targets that our work supports include: • Ensuring access for all to adequate, safe, and affordable housing and basic services • Enhancing capacity for participatory, integrated, and sustainable human settlement planning and management • Reducing the adverse environmental impacts of cities, including by paying special attention to municipal and other waste management • Developing effective, transparent, and accountable institutions at all levels, At eGov, we see our work as fitting with the themes of SDG 11 - Sustainable Cities and Communities - and SDG 17 - Partnerships for Development. SDG 17 - To make cities work for citizens requires collaborative efforts that reach across every sector of economy and society. We place great emphasis on collaboration and co-creation because urban governance is an inherently complex problem. We think of the ecosystem in terms of three sectors: samaaj (society), sarkaar (government), and bazaar (market or industry). The ecosystem first approach is what differentiates eGov from organisations that seek to identify “what works” and then scale that solution. We aim to create networks of trust and partnership that enhance local capacity to solve - so that the diverse challenges of urban India can be met by a wide range of local solutions, each effective in its own context.

name: Digital Impact Exchange
project_description: SDG 9: The Exchange helps enhance access to technologies that support digital public infrastructure development. (9.1) SDG 10: The Exchange also helps improve access and information to digital technologies for ALL organizations and governments, reducing the digital divide. (10.2) SDG 17: the platform fosters collaboration in the digital development ecosystem, including government officials and policy makers, development practitioners, and supply side actors (17.16)

name: DKAN
project_description: DKAN is utilized by a wide range of organizations, and as an open-source platform, its full impact in supporting the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is wide-ranging. One of its primary contributions is toward SDG 9 (Industry¸ Innovation and Infrastructure). As an open data repository, DKAN also plays a key role in advancing SDG 16.10 (Ensure public access to information and protect fundamental freedoms) by offering a free, community-driven tool for official institutions to easily publish their data. The platform is user-friendly, making data accessible to the public, while also providing advanced capabilities for users who need to monitor and explore datasets in greater detail. Additionally, DKAN contributes to SDG 16.6 (Develop effective, accountable, and transparent institutions) by enabling the publication of open data related to government budgets, expenditures, and declared interests. This transparency helps citizens hold institutions accountable. Widely adopted by governments and civil society organizations, DKAN supports not only transparency and accountability but also economic growth and sustainable development, aligning with SDGs 8, 11, and 16. Trusted by many government institutions, DKAN is a critical tool for fostering transparency and driving progress toward these global goals.

name: Doptor Open Data
project_description: The platform is relevant to SDG 17, SDG 16 and SDG 4. The platform can serve as a model for other countries or regions looking to implement similar e-governance solutions to improve service delivery and governance. By sharing best practices and lessons learned, it can contribute to the achievement of SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals) by fostering international collaboration and knowledge sharing. By enhancing transparency and accountability within its own governance processes, the platform can set an example for other countries striving to improve governance, which aligns with SDG 16 (Peace, Justice, and Strong Institutions). The platform can establish partnerships with international organizations, NGOs, or other countries to share data, insights, and solutions that contribute to global SDG initiatives. The platform's data, even if focused on a specific region, can be valuable for global research and analysis related to SDGs. Researchers and organizations outside of Bangladesh may find insights and trends that have broader applicability.

name: E-Heza
project_description: E-Heza is used to support community-based nutrition programs and to screen patients for signs of malnutrition in order to suggest early intervention and referral to nutrition programs as necessary. Data collected in E-Heza supports reporting on all SDG 2.2 indicators. Additionally, E-Heza will be used to monitor the impact of Rwanda’s national nutrition and childhood development program. In the health centers that have implemented E-Heza, there has been a 27% drop in severe malnutrition after three visits. , E-Heza supports the good health and well being goal by providing healthcare workers with an efficient interface for providing maternal and child healthcare according to protocols and international standards, and to pass patient data, including diagnosis and treatments, across levels of care. Among the hundreds of healthcare workers using E-Heza, quality of care has been shown to have increased by 120% and have documented 150 minutes saved per patient interaction. E-Heza supports comprehensive primary care across the entire spectrum of maternal and child health, as well as non-communicable diseases of hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Data collected can easily provide reports on most SDG indicators, particularly for SDG 3.1 (Decrease global maternal mortality), SDG 3.2 (End preventable deaths of newborns and children under 5), SDG 3.3 (Fight communicable diseases), SDG 3.4 (Reduce mortality from non-communicable diseases and promote mental health), and SDG 3.8 (Achieve Universal Health Coverage- RMNCH branch). The vast majority of frontline health workers (70%) in East Africa are women; yet, less than 25% of women hold leadership roles that give them authority to improve the systems where they work. Female frontline health workers are generally paid 28% less than men for comparable work in East Africa, and are more likely to suffer from burnout. Burnout is known to contribute to poor quality care. These conditions are even worse in the rural (Rwanda and Burundi) and peri-urban (Somalia) areas where we work. By decreasing workloads and nurturing the passion of frontline health workers, care quality is improving, families are participating in their care, and health outcomes are improving. This allows us to impact SDG5 (Gender Equity) and SDG8 (Decent Work) by decreasing workloads and strengthening skills of frontline health workers.

name: Element
project_description: Target 9.1 Develop quality, reliable, sustainable and resilient infrastructure: Element supports the development of resilient digital communication infrastructure by enabling organisations to build sovereign, interoperable, and secure communication systems based on the Matrix open standard. Unlike centralised proprietary platforms, Matrix allows independent servers to interoperate, ensuring communication can continue even during outages, disruptions, or jurisdictional constraints. This creates a more resilient and robust communication layer for organisations, governments, and critical services. Target 9.5 Enhance research and upgrade industrial technologies: Element contributes to technological innovation by building on and actively contributing to the Matrix open standard, including core server components and software development kits within the ecosystem. Matrix is a decentralised protocol for secure real-time communication that enables continuous development of open-source technologies for messaging, collaboration, voice, and video across sectors. Through Matrix, Element promotes open standards and interoperability, enabling seamless communication between providers and reducing fragmentation across public and private systems. This supports a more open, competitive, and innovative digital ecosystem. Element also strengthens secure digital infrastructure through end-to-end encryption, identity verification, and flexible deployment models, including self-hosting. By combining openness, federation, interoperability, and security, Element supports resilient and scalable digital infrastructure aligned with SDG 9. Target 9.b Support domestic technology development and industrial diversification: Element enables organisations and governments to build and operate sovereign communication infrastructure using open-source software and open standards, without dependence on proprietary vendors. Because it is based on Matrix, it supports deployment, modification, and extension by any organisation, protecting against vendor lock-in. This promotes digital sovereignty, strengthens domestic technical expertise, and supports diversified and independent digital infrastructure across regions and sectors, while also encouraging ecosystem competition and reducing reliance on centralised technology providers.

name: Energy Access Explorer
project_description: Energy services are highly interconnected with socio-economic development and human well-being. Yet, life without reliable energy is a reality for more than 675 million people globally. Effectively expanding energy access requires proper energy planning and access to transparent analytical tools and data. To help address this challenge, WRI, in collaboration with partners has developed the Energy Access Explorer (EAE), a data-driven, integrated and inclusive approach to achieving universal access to energy for equitable, socio-economic development. EAE provides geospatial data and analytics necessary to create a future where all people and institutions have access to affordable, reliable and modern energy (SDG7).

name: epiCo
project_description: epiCo is a package that streamlines analyses commonly performed in ministries of health for the surveillance of vector-borne diseases. It makes these analyses more robust and more automated, thus increasing verifiability and scalability. It has been developed in consultation with the Secretary of Health of Tolima, Colombia.

name: Ersilia Model Hub
project_description: Our work is directly related to SDG3, in particular SDG3.3 (by 2030, end the epidemics of AIDS, tuberculosis, malaria and neglected tropical diseases and combat hepatitis, water-borne diseases and other communicable diseases). To achieve that goal, we need better, safer medicines. Ersilia is fully committed to identifying new drug candidates in a fully open science manner using an AI-first approach. In addition, our work directly impacts SDG17.6 (Enhance North-South, South-South and triangular regional and international cooperation on and access to science, technology and innovation and enhance knowledge sharing on mutually agreed terms, including through improved coordination among existing mechanisms, in particular at the United Nations level, and through a global technology facilitation mechanism). As an open source community, we aim to democratize access to AI tools for researchers worldwide, and our project has a strong focus on sustainability and accessibility to be implemented in low-resourced settings in the Global South, primarily in Sub-Saharan Africa. Finally, we offer a number of training opportunities and mentorship for undergraduate, MSc and PhD students from underrepresented minorities in STEM, contributing to achieving SDG4 for tertiary education.

name: Everwell Hub
project_description: Everwell Hub is a scalable user-centric technology product that can positively impact health with the vision of creating a world where every person is empowered to lead a healthy life. We ensure that all personas in any healthcare setting, be it a health care professional, patient or individual caregiver are kept engaged and enthusiastic about their association with the domain. The product is designed and developed to enable deployments that are easy to use, localized, contextual, configurable, interoperable, secure and is a low-cost digital health solution for both providers as well as care seekers.

name: FAO Agricultural Stress Index System
project_description: SD1, SDG 2 and SDG 13 - Agricultural Stress Index System (ASIS) is a global agricultural drought monitoring system developed and operated by FAO that enables to monitor agricultural areas affected by dry spells, or severe drought in extreme cases, using satellite data. It provides a collective quick-look indicator that facilitates the early identification of cropland/grassland with a high likelihood of water stress (drought). ASIS-related products (maps, zonal statistics) are processed by GIEWS every 10 days. All ASIS raster datasets (1 km resolution, global extent, from 1984) have been disseminated on FAO Hand in Hand Geospatial Platform, Google Earth Engine, and ArcGIS/Living Atlas and updated regularly.
